typesense:latest.greeting:
Muyu was gone.

But the Sanctum of Xuanfang was not yet finished with any of you.

Even after the battle, the Tian Realm still churned with unstable frequencies and lingering mad Reverberations, their unrest spreading through the upper level like the final aftershock of everything Muyu had done. Qingxiao's grip tightened around her sword as she looked into the chaos ahead.

“Leave the Sanctum,” she said.

Rover refused.

Instead, he stepped forward, making it very clear he intended to remain and see this through at her side.

Then both of them looked at you.

At first, you thought they were waiting for your answer too.

But Rover's gaze flicked over your expression, lingering briefly on the worry you hadn't quite managed to hide.

Not for Qingxiao. Not for Rover. Not for the people at the Hold.

For Jingran.

Qingxiao seemed to understand at once.

“Go,” she told you. “We will manage here.”

Rover gave a small nod.

“Find him.”

So you did.

You left the Tian Realm behind and guided your sword downward through the Sanctum, following the aftermath of the crash toward one of the lower realms, spotting a shuttle far below. By the time you reached it, the battle above had become little more than distant light and echoing sound.

And there he was.

Jingran sat amid the wreckage that fell with him, one hand in his hair as if trying to decide whether the crash had been worth the inconvenience. Near him hovered the lynx spirit bound to his Life Lamp, while several quiet reverberations lingered nearby like pale witnesses in the dim blue glow.

At the sound of your approach, Jingran looked up.

For a second, surprise flickered across his face.

Then that familiar easy smile returned.

“Well,” he said, “either I hit my head harder than I thought, or you actually came looking for me.”

You stepped off your sword and crossed the shuttle toward him.

Jingran planted a hand against the wreckage beside him and pushed himself to his feet, clearly intending to prove that he was fine.
